codex.text:
1. The persistence count (two scans) is a free parameter with no stated selection procedure — tuning it against the same sealed holdout until the ≥10% bar clears contaminates the holdout and is textbook multiple-testing overfitting; the criterion also omits any minimum sample size or significance test, so a 10% relative expectancy delta on a thin holdout is indistinguishable from noise.
2. "No increase in trade costs" is unmeasurable as written: costs are runner spread/slippage assumptions, and a double-scan delay changes trade timing and frequency, so per-trade cost parity says nothing about aggregate cost drag — specify cost-normalized expectancy net of realized frequency instead.
3. Validation gaps: no ExperimentRegistry requirement, no regime/subsample breakdown for cases where the first scan fires but the second doesn't, and no analysis of edge decay during the inter-scan wait — delayed entry can systematically buy worse prices, which the raw expectancy comparison would misattribute.
4. "No increase in maximum drawdown" is confounded because the filter trades less (fewer trades mechanically shrink DD), and any acceptance must still route through the full `bot/aegis/research/promote.py` gate suite via `research_promote_champion.py` — the proposal never says so, leaving an ad hoc promotion path open.

Two correlated scans do not establish persistence; this can overfit scan cadence and silently delay entries into worse prices. A 10% holdout threshold is meaningless without confidence intervals, sample-size requirements, locked cost/slippage assumptions, and multiple-testing control. “No increase” in drawdown or costs needs precise measurement windows, and the filter must not bypass any existing DEMO execution, risk, OMS, or invalidation gates.

hermes.text: Spread percentiles may proxy for volatile sessions, news, symbols, or signal quality, so bucket differences cannot establish that spread abstention itself improves EV. “Significant” is undefined and top-quartile samples may be too small or repeatedly sliced, creating selection bias without pre-specified confidence intervals, minimum sample sizes, and time-ordered out-of-sample splits. The proposal also needs validation that the trailing percentile is computed only from information available at entry and remains stable across symbols and regimes; sealed-holdout promotion is appropriate, and no direct safety violation is proposed.

The retrospective outcome log is vulnerable to regime and selection bias: “own trailing distribution,” window, minimum sample size, percentile computation, and spread measurement are unspecified, and using the full log risks contaminating the sealed holdout. The rule also lacks pre-registered statistical thresholds, confidence intervals, multiple-comparison control, and a test that aggregate net EV improves after accounting for abstained trade volume, so “remaining buckets stay positive” can be meaningless under low power. No direct safety violation is proposed, but the shadow phase needs explicit isolation from the sole MT5 execution owner and proof that the gate cannot mutate runner, config, or champion state.

opencode.text: The 20%/90% bands, 15-minute timeframe, and 60-day window are three unpenalized degrees of freedom with no stated selection protocol — if they were picked after seeing holdout results, the "sealed" holdout is already burned, and nothing prevents iterative threshold-tuning against the same sealed set across repeated challenger attempts (no multiple-testing control or holdout rotation). The acceptance tests are statistically vacuous as written: "net expectancy improves" specifies no minimum effect size or significance test (e.g., bootstrap CI on per-trade net PnL), "no increase in maximum drawdown" allows no tolerance band despite drawdown being a high-variance estimator at n≈100, and "100 qualifying trades" never defines "qualifying." Missing validation: explicit point-in-time proof that the trailing percentile uses only decision-time data (lookahead risk), a paired same-entry comparison against the baseline so any delta is attributable to the filter rather than differing trade samples, and walk-forward or multi-regime coverage so one historical volatility regime can't manufacture the result. Finally, the proposal omits mandatory ExperimentRegistry logging (AGENTS.md rule 4), so even a pass would be an unrecorded experiment.

The fixed 20%/90% thresholds and 60-day window are arbitrary tuning choices that invite overfitting, especially if many variants were tried before selecting this proposal. “Improves net expectancy” lacks a minimum effect size, confidence interval, significance/multiple-testing correction, and rules for incomplete or correlated trades; 100 trades alone is not adequate validation. It also does not require point-in-time percentile computation, preregistration and ExperimentRegistry recording, walk-forward or multi-period robustness checks, or explicit confirmation that the challenger cannot bypass governed promotion and DEMO-only execution controls.

proposals.text: Candidate improvement: a spread-percentile abstention gate, tested shadow-first before any code change. Hypothesis: entries opened when the live spread at signal time falls in the top quartile of its own trailing distribution realize materially lower (possibly negative) mean net-of-cost EV than lower-quartile entries, so abstaining on them raises aggregate expectancy. Method: retrospectively bucket confirmed trades in the existing outcome_log.jsonl by entry-spread percentile, compare net expectancy, hit rate, and tail loss across buckets, and log the study in ExperimentRegistry — analysis only, no runner, config, or champion edits. Decision rule (falsifiable): advance to a shadow validation gate only if top-quartile net expectancy is negative while the remaining buckets stay positive, and then require the gated policy to beat the ungated intelligent champion on sealed holdout data through all promote.py gates before any champion update. If the buckets show no significant expectancy difference, record the null honestly and drop the candidate for the cycle.

Test a volatility-regime filter that abstains when the current 15-minute ATR percentile is below 20% or above 90% of its trailing 60-day distribution. Evaluate it only on sealed historical holdouts with the runner’s existing spread/slippage assumptions, comparing net expectancy, drawdown, and trade count against the unchanged validated-state baseline. Accept it as a challenger only if net expectancy improves with no increase in maximum drawdown and at least 100 qualifying trades.

Test a two-consecutive-scan persistence filter: permit a DEMO Firehose entry only when the validated-state gate remains valid on both scans. Accept the candidate only if sealed holdout results show at least a 10% improvement in net expectancy with no increase in maximum drawdown or trade costs versus the current champion; otherwise reject it and keep the champion unchanged.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

codex.text: Pre-register the persistence count and scan cadence in `ExperimentRegistry`, select them only on a development set with multiplicity control, and evaluate once on an untouched sealed holdout with a minimum trade count and confidence intervals demonstrating a statistically supported ≥10% improvement in cost-normalized net expectancy. Measure expectancy using locked runner spread/slippage assumptions and realized trade frequency, while reporting inter-scan price deterioration, edge decay, and regime/subsample outcomes for candidates that pass the first scan but fail the second. Compare drawdown over identical calendar and exposure windows, alongside trade count, turnover, and aggregate cost drag, rather than relying on raw maximum drawdown or per-trade cost parity. Any accepted challenger must pass the complete `bot/aegis/research/promote.py` gate suite through `research_promote_champion.py`; otherwise retain the champion and preserve all existing DEMO execution, risk, quote, OMS, invalidation, and account-safety gates.

hermes.text: Candidate improvement: a spread-percentile abstention gate, tested shadow-first before any code change. Hypothesis: entries opened when live spread at signal time falls in the top quartile of a pre-registered trailing distribution — per-symbol, trailing 30 days of signal-time spreads with a minimum of 100 observations, computed strictly point-in-time from data available at entry — realize materially lower mean net-of-cost EV than lower-quartile entries, enough that abstaining raises aggregate net expectancy even after forfeiting the skipped trades' positive-EV volume. Method: retrospectively bucket confirmed trades in outcome_log.jsonl using exactly that frozen definition, excluding all sealed-holdout periods from estimation, with a single pre-registered primary contrast (top vs. bottom quartile, two-sided bootstrap 95% CI, minimum 200 confirmed trades per bucket), time-ordered train/validation splits, Holm correction on any secondary slices, and confound diagnostics stratifying by session hour, symbol, scheduled-news windows, and signal type to demonstrate a residual spread effect rather than a volatility/session proxy. Decision rule (falsifiable): advance to shadow validation only if the top-quartile net-expectancy CI lies wholly below zero, the bottom-quartile CI lies above zero, the sign pattern replicates out-of-sample and across symbols/regimes without flips, and simulated abstention beats the realized trade book on aggregate net EV after charging skipped winners — otherwise record the null honestly in ExperimentRegistry and drop the candidate for the cycle. Any resulting shadow gate runs as a read-only research process fully isolated from the sole MT5 execution owner, writing nothing but its own study artifacts under bot/reports/research/ — never runner, config, or champion state. Champion adoption still requires the gated policy to beat the ungated intelligent champion on sealed holdout data through every promote.py gate before any champion update.

opencode.text: Preregister the 15-minute ATR percentile filter, including the 20%/90% bands and 60-day trailing window, in `ExperimentRegistry` before execution; compute every percentile strictly from data available at each decision time. Evaluate the filter as a paired abstention overlay on identical validated-state baseline entry opportunities across sealed, rotated holdouts and walk-forward periods spanning multiple volatility regimes, using existing spread/slippage assumptions. Define qualifying trades as baseline-authorized entries with complete outcome data after costs, require at least 100 retained trades per evaluation period, and report block-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for paired per-trade net-PnL differences to address serial correlation. Accept only if the aggregate paired expectancy improvement is at least a preregistered minimum effect size with a multiplicity-adjusted lower confidence bound above zero, and maximum drawdown does not exceed the baseline by more than a preregistered tolerance. Record all variants, failures, and results in the registry; submit any passing result only through governed champion promotion, with no change to DEMO-only execution controls.
